newsitem.title: FRANCE: Exiles say mercenaries in action in east Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Exiles say mercenaries in action in east Zaire.

text.p: A Zairean opposition group alleged on Friday that mercenaries had gone into action against rebels in east Zaire, killing and shelling civilians.

The Paris-based Coordination of the Zairean Diaspora's Democratic Organisations (CODEZAD) accused the mercenaries of following in the footsteps of their predecessors who fought African wars in the 1960s by raping women, bayoneting children and mutilating men.
"No-one will be entitled tomorrow to say he ignored this horror which started with the shelling of civilian populations in Walikale," it said.

Zaire said earlier this month its troops had recaptured the town of Walikale in a counteroffensive against Rwanda-backed rebels who have captured a swathe of eastern Zaire. There had been no independent confirmation that the town had fallen to the rebels.
CODEZAD said the mercenaries included men from France. Belgium, China, Egypt and Kuwait.
The Federation of African Workers in France (FETAF) issued a statement expressing surprise that member countries of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) had remained silent about the mercenaries.
There have been various reports of mercenaries gathering in east Zaire to bolster the troops of President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The left-wing French daily Liberation said some 280 European soldiers of fortune were under the command of a veteran Belgian mercenary.
It said the force included many Serbs and Croats as well as others from Russia, Poland, France, Belgium and Italy.

France has denied any connection with, or knowledge of the mercenaries and said it had no military cooperation with Zaire and scrupulously respected a European Union embargo on supplies of weapons to the region.
